subject: PO term flexibility and buyer approval gaps
messages:
From: Tom Raines <traines@acmehealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Offer — term questions before internal review

Neha — thanks for the quick overview on the call earlier. A couple of items procurement wants clarified before we route the PO for signature: 

1) Our CFO is looking for a split option: one-year annual commitment for core cluster plus a usage bucket for burst/experimental workloads. Can Redwood issue a private offer that separates the annual commitment from the pay-as-you-go portion in the Marketplace purchase?

2) Who is the single approver required on the Acme side? Procurement says this will need procurement + BU finance + security (three signoffs). That will add at least a week in our process. Any ideas on how to speed that?

We'd like to try to keep the activation window under 10 business days if possible.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Raines
Head of Cloud Procurement — AcmeHealth
procurement@acmehealth.com

Attachment: approval-roster-acme.xlsx (spreadsheet with approver names and roles)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Raines <traines@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer — term questions before internal review

Tom — really appreciate the clarity. Short answers below, and I copied Vanessa (Marketplace) + Vivek (Sales Ops) to scope what we can do on the PO structure and activation timeline.

- Term split: Yes — AWS private offers can be structured with a reserved annual commitment line item plus a separate usage line for metered consumption. We'll need to model the pricing tiers so the annual commit excludes metered usage; Vanessa, can you confirm the SKU split and pricing cadence?

- Approvers: On Redwood's side, we can put an activation gating rule that requires buyer acceptance and the PO signature. If Acme requires procurement + BU finance + security, that will be reflected in your approval roster and will affect activation timing. Two options to speed things up: 1) Use an internal delegated approver (single person authorized to sign on behalf of BU finance), or 2) Request an expedited activation flag from AWS (we can help request seller-initiated activation). Both require buyer-side consent.

- Activation window: If we get all signatures and the PO activated via Seller Accept on AWS within the same day, activation can be ~48 hours; with a 3-5 day internal approval window it will be longer.

Next step: Vanessa, Vivek — can you look at the attached draft PO (RDW-Acme_PO-draft-v3.pdf) and confirm whether we can create a multi-line private offer and an expedited activation request to AWS? I'll ask Acme if they can nominate a delegated signer to help compress approvals.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0147

Attachment: RDW-Acme_PO-draft-v3.pdf (private offer draft; redlined sections for term and SKU split)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Tom Raines <traines@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer — term questions before internal review

Tom / Neha — quick ops note after reviewing the draft:

- SKU split: We can create two SKUs under a single private offer: RDW-CORE-ANNUAL (annual reserved vCPU/GPU commitment) and RDW-EXP-METER (metered tokens/embeddings). Pricing model: annual SKU priced as committed monthly spend; metered SKU at published pay-as-you-go rate. We'll document the exclusion rule (annual commitment does not apply to metered charges).

- Billing & activation: AWS requires the seller to accept the private offer; activation then follows buyer-side purchase acceptance. If Acme's approval is multi-signer, the PO will be stuck until the buyer executes. We can submit an AWS support ticket to request a manual expedite on activation (seller-initiated). That usually shortens acceptance processing time but doesn't replace buyer signatures.

- Approver mapping: Jordan, can you check whether we've previously used delegated signers for Acme-sized customers (enterprise finance delegation)? If yes, we can include language in the offer to support that flow.

Operational ask for Acme: if you can identify 1 delegated signer or provide a procurement SFTP with signed authorization, we can try to compress the flow.

Vanessa Ortiz
Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

---

Thanks all — very helpful. Acme is prepared to: 

- Nominate a delegated signer from BU finance (I'll confirm name by EOD tomorrow).
- Accept the two-line SKU split as proposed; procurement wants the annual commitment to show as a distinct line item on the AWS invoice.
- We submitted the internal approval roster (see attached) and asked for security signoff by next Wednesday.

Two operational asks for Redwood: 
1) Please provide the SKUs and the final pricing table so I can attach them to the procurement submission. Ideally a CSV or a single-line table we can paste into our PO system.
2) Can your team open the expedite request with AWS once the delegated signer is confirmed? If you include the HubSpot link with the AWS case it helps speed the internal AWS routing.

I'll circulate the final delegated signer and confirm timing. Appreciate the quick collaboration.

—Tom
